statement: The Norman Conquest (1066) created an inseparable link between the Duchy of Normandy and the Kingdom of England: William I and his heirs ruled both simultaneously. The relationship created the 'English problem' in French feudal law — the King of England was simultaneously a vassal of the French crown for Normandy. This dual status generated permanent tension: English kings built military resources in England to defend or recover their French possessions; the French crown treated English kings' French fiefs as a permanent source of legal leverage. The dynamic drove Anglo-French relations for 150 years until Philip II Augustus conquered Normandy (1204).
